title: Add migration staleness detector and release-lockfile pinning for safer operator upgrades
author: Aisha Rao
body:
Summary: This PR adds a lightweight migration staleness detector to the private operator, and introduces a release-lockfile format that pins the operator image, migration set hash, and helm/tf module checksums. Motivation: we observed two customer incidents where an out-of-order upgrade (operator image updated before migrations finished) caused schema drift and prolonged recovery. The operator does not currently surface a deterministic check that a cluster's migrations match the incoming release. This change reduces blast radius by failing upgrades early when migrations appear stale, and by making release pinning explicit in the operator helm values and terraform module outputs.

What changed (high-level):
- operator: add MigrationStalenessChecker run during the pre-upgrade hook; it inspects the db migration history table (migration_id + applied_at) and compares against the release-lockfile's migration set hash. If mismatch and exceeded staleness window, operator will pause the rollout and emit an event/metric.
- release-lockfile: new YAML manifest format (release-lock.yaml) that contains image:tag, migration_set_hash (sha256 of migration manifests), helm_chart_checksum, terraform_module_checksum, signed_by (PGP key id). The operator validates the lockfile signature if verifyLockfile is enabled.
- helm chart: add values for releaseLockfile.enabled, releaseLockfile.path, verifyLockfile, and migrationStaleness.windowMinutes. Add a pre-upgrade hook that runs the migration-check job when enabled.
- terraform module: expose release_lockfile output and add an option to upload lockfile to customer-backed object store (S3/GCS) for airgapped installs.
- migration-runner: expose --compute-migration-hash to generate the migration_set_hash used by the lockfile. Also added a dry-run mode that performs a schema-only plan and returns a deterministic exit code for the operator to use.
- docs: upgrade playbook additions, sample release-lockfile, and troubleshooting section for staleness situations.

Checklist (implemented):
- [x] migration-set hashing and runner flag
- [x] release-lockfile spec and helm values
- [x] operator pre-upgrade staleness detector with configurable window and soft-fail mode
- [x] lockfile signature verification support
- [x] terraform outputs to surface lockfile references
- [x] docs and example lockfile template
- [x] unit tests + integration smoke test in perf-canary harness

How it works (workflow):
1) Release engineer runs migration-runner --compute-migration-hash against the migrations/ directory to get migration_set_hash and produces release-lock.yaml (can be signed).
2) Lockfile is uploaded to customer object store or included in the helm chart values for private installs.
3) When the operator receives the new chart/image, it loads the lockfile (local or remote). If verifyLockfile=true it verifies signature.
4) Operator queries the DB migration table and computes current cluster migration_set_hash. If hashes mismatch and the most recent applied migration is older than migrationStaleness.windowMinutes, operator raises an event and pauses the upgrade. The operator emits metric redwood_private_upgrade_migration_staleness{cluster="..."} with a reason label.
5) To proceed, an operator/admin may run the migration-runner in dry-run/plan mode and/or apply incremental migrations, then re-run the upgrade.

Rollback/Canary behavior:
- If an upgrade is paused due to staleness, operator supports an override annotation redwood.io/force-upgrade=true but only when verifyLockfile=false and cluster is marked as dev/test. This is gated to prevent accidental production bypasses.
- Canary rollouts still respect lockfile pinning; the operator will only allow a canary to progress if the migration_set_hash matches or the staleness window hasn't been exceeded for that canary subset.

Safety guarantees and limitations:
- This is a guard, not a full transactional migration system. It prevents obvious mismatches and long-stale clusters from silently drifting, but does not auto-apply migrations.
- For airgapped customers, we provide tooling to upload signed lockfiles to S3/GCS and terraform outputs to reference them.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for hash computation and operator detection logic.
- Integration test in perf-canary that simulates: (a) fresh cluster (pass path), (b) cluster with pending migrations within window (soft pass), (c) cluster with old pending migrations (fail/pause).
- Manual verification of helm pre-upgrade hook and terraform reference.

Release notes: This change adds a pre-upgrade migration staleness check and a release-lockfile pin to assistance safer private upgrades. It is opt-in by default for existing installs; new installs from the updated chart will have staleness checks enabled.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: merge to main, enable in perf canary for 2 weeks.
- Stage 2: enable for non-critical customer clusters (flagged by customer tag) and collect metrics/alerts.
- Stage 3: default enable for all private installs in next minor release after metrics review.

Operational runbook excerpt: If a cluster is paused by staleness detector: 1) Inspect redwood_private_upgrade_migration_staleness events, 2) Run migration-runner --plan to verify pending migrations, 3) Apply migrations or regenerate lockfile, 4) re-run helm upgrade. If immediate rollback is required, follow the standard rollback playbook — migration-runner outputs include migration_id markers to assist rollbacks.

Related work: ENG-4721 (migration observability), ENG-4789 (release pinning proposal).

Contact: @aisha for rollout coordination and playbook additions.
commits: chore(helm): add releaseLockfile values and pre-upgrade job (e7f89ab)
feat(terraform): expose release_lockfile outputs and upload option (c9d0123)
docs: add release-lockfile spec and upgrade playbook (b8c7d6e)
review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice end-to-end. A few nits: make staleness window default to 48h not 24h; prefer telemetry label 'reason' to be short codes.
Aisha Rao: Updated default to 48h and added short reason codes (mismatch, stale, unsigned). PTAL.
Priya Kapoor: Can we ensure signature verification failure doesn't brick operator in airgapped installs? Suggest default verifyLockfile=false and explicit opt-in.
Aisha Rao: verifyLockfile=false by default; added terraform helper to upload signed lockfile for airgapped installs.
ci_log: ci/integration(perf-canary): initial run failed (timeout on migration test), rerun passed
notes_for_ops: Operators should add release-lockfile when doing private upgrades. Use migration-runner --compute-migration-hash to produce migration_set_hash and include it in release-lock.yaml. If using airgapped installs, upload signed lockfile to the object store and reference via terraform output 'release_lockfile_url'.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in pre-upgrade migration staleness detector and a release-lockfile format to pin operator image and migration set. Default enabled for new installs; existing clusters opt-in. Improves safety for private/on-prem upgrades.
